---
title: "`ev_app()` — interactive GUI launcher"
---

## Purpose

Launch the bundled Shiny app to load differential abundance results, pick
databases and thresholds, and render the volcano-in-ring composite
interactively.

## When to use

For exploratory work or demos when you want to sweep databases and cutoffs
without editing a script. Reach for the scripted functions
([`ev_enrich`](ev_enrich.qmd), [`ev_volcano_ring`](ev_volcano_ring.qmd)) when you
need reproducible, version-controlled figures.

## How it works

Checks that the `shiny` package is installed — it is **Suggests-only**, so the
core package works without it and the launcher aborts with an install hint if
it is missing. It then locates the app bundled at `inst/shiny/` and hands off to
`shiny::runApp()`. Extra arguments in `...` (e.g. `launch.browser`, `port`) are
forwarded to `runApp()`. The function returns `NULL` invisibly; it is called for
its side effect of running the app.

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `...` | *(none)* | forwarded to `shiny::runApp()` (`launch.browser`, `port`, …) |

## Literature

No method-specific citation; see [methods](../methods.qmd).

## Example

```r
# install.packages("shiny")   # Suggests-only dependency
ev_app()                       # open in default viewer
ev_app(launch.browser = TRUE, port = 8080)
```
